text:
Olivia P.: Heads-up — starting phased rollout of v2 to 15% in us-east in ~10m. Release notes updated: https://redwood.example/release/v2-notes :eyes:

deploy-bot: Deploy v2 -> us-east starting: 3712468000 | target 15% traffic

Mike L.: seeing a few mobile SDKs still sending `X-Client-Version: v1` — looks like older SDKs. 3 distinct client IDs so far.

QA-Bot: Telemetry alert: latency p50 +40ms and error rate +1.8% on /v2/generate from 3712468045

QA-Bot: logs:
```
2026-03-20T14:20:55Z ERROR handler.go:142 client=mobile-app-31 X-Client-Version=v1 upstream=400
```

Sam (mobile): confirmed — our SDK 3.2.1 has a header mapping regression. We can ship a patch but won't be instantaneous.

Arpit S.: Suggest we throttle back to 5% and enable header fallback where `X-Client-Version=v1` routes to v1. That avoids a full rollback and limits impact.

Jess H.: +1. Proposed rollback criteria: error rate >2.5% for 5m OR sustained user-facing errors across >3 regions -> immediate rollback. Also recommend pinning top-10 customers while we patch the SDK.

Olivia P.: agree. @deploy-bot hold rollout and change target to 5%.

deploy-bot: Action: reduce v2 traffic to 5% in us-east — initiated (3712468072) :hourglass_flowing_sand:

Mike L.: Can we apply header fallback config? example rule:
```
route:
  - if: header['X-Client-Version']=='v1'
    route: v1
  - else:
    route: v2
```

Arpit S.: I'll push the route change and add a canary rule for the top-10 client IDs (customer pins).

deploy-bot: Route config update deployed (3712468105). Traffic now 5%. Monitoring...

QA-Bot: After change: p50 back to normal, error rate down to +0.3% (3712468120) :white_check_mark:

Olivia P.: Good. Keep the hold for 1 hour and continue targeted customer outreach. Update release notes with a compatibility caveat and rollback instructions.

Jess H.: I'll draft a short addendum for the release notes and post to #support and #customer-success.

deploy-bot: Thread status: rollout held at 5% — awaiting SDK patch and customer confirmations. (closing summary added)
